description.notes: The data are aggregated daily repurchase agreement volumes transacted via the Fixed Income Clearing Corporation’s (FICC) sponsored repo platform. Sponsored repos are secured borrowing transactions where FICC-member dealers sponsor non-dealer counterparties (e.g., hedge funds) that need to borrow cash. Sponsored reverse repos are secured borrowing transactions where FICC-member dealers sponsor non-dealer counterparties (e.g., money market funds) that want to lend cash. Sponsored repo and reverse repo transactions are centrally cleared via FICC’s sponsored platform. Hedge funds borrowing cash comprise the majority of sponsored repo volumes, whereas money market funds lending cash comprise the majority of sponsored reverse repo volumes. See additional definitions and methodology on the Sponsored Repo Data Sets page of the Hedge Fund Monitor.

description.notes: The data are derived from responses to question 9 of the Federal Reserve Board’s quarterly Senior Credit Officer Opinion Survey on Dealer Financing Terms (SCOOS). The net percent represents the fraction of dealers reporting an increase—either "considerably" or "somewhat"—in the availability of leverage offered to hedge funds minus those reporting a decrease. A positive net percent indicates an overall increase in the availability of leverage compared with the prior quarter, while a negative net percent indicates an overall decrease over the same period. See additional definitions and methodology on the SCOOS Data Sets page of the Hedge Fund Monitor.

description.notes: The data are derived from responses to question 10 of the Federal Reserve Board’s quarterly Senior Credit Officer Opinion Survey on Dealer Financing Terms (SCOOS). The net percent represents the fraction of dealers reporting an increase—either 'considerably’ or ‘somewhat’—in the provision of differential terms offered to their most-favored hedge fund clients minus those reporting a decrease. A positive net percent indicates that the terms provided by dealers to their most-favored hedge fund clients have become more beneficial relative to the average hedge fund client compared with the prior quarter, while a negative net percent indicates the terms provided to all hedge fund clients have become more similar. See additional definitions and methodology on the SCOOS Data Sets page of the Hedge Fund Monitor.

unit.name: Net percent of respondents reporting a change

description.notes: The data are derived from responses to question 7 of the Federal Reserve Board’s quarterly Senior Credit Officer Opinion Survey on Dealer Financing Terms (SCOOS). The net percent represents the fraction of dealers reporting that hedge funds increased—either "considerably" or "somewhat"—the intensity of their efforts to negotiate better credit terms minus those reporting a decrease. A positive net percent indicates overall greater efforts by hedge funds to negotiate better credit terms compared with the prior quarter, while a negative net percent indicates an overall reduction in efforts over the same period. See additional definitions and methodology on the SCOOS Data Sets page of the Hedge Fund Monitor.

description.notes: The data are compiled from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Traders in Financial Futures (TFF) combined options and futures report. The 10-year equivalent positions are calculated by scaling the number of contracts held by the ratio of the dollar value of a one basis point change in yield (DV01) of the contract and the DV01 of the 10-year Treasury futures contract and multiplying by the notional value of the contract. Deliverable securities for the 10-year Treasury futures contract have a remaining term to maturity of at least 6 years and 6 months, but less than eight years. Leveraged funds are typically hedge funds and various types of money managers, including registered commodity trading advisors (CTAs), registered commodity pool operators (CPOs), or unregistered funds identified by the CFTC.
